points.t: Flat, evenly brown macules on the face or backs of the hands of an older outdoor worker that do not fade in winter.
Chronic UV increases local melanocyte number and activity along elongated rete ridges.
Photoprotection forever; topical retinoids/azelaic acid for modest fading; cryotherapy/IPL/laser only after cancer exclusion — usually private.
Irregular, multicoloured, enlarging facial pigment → lentigo maligna — urgent suspected-cancer referral. Never laser an undiagnosed pigmented lesion.

points: Uniform light-to-dark brown macules with a regular border; face, dorsal hands, forearms, shoulders.
May coexist with AK field change and photoageing.

cards.name: Melasma
cards.clue: Symmetrical patches; hormones; worsened by heat/IPL — see [melasma](condition:melasma-facial-melanosis)

cards.name: Lentigo maligna
cards.clue: Irregular colours, slow enlargement on older face → NG12 referral

items.t: Any lesion suspicious for lentigo maligna or melanoma → urgent suspected-cancer pathway.
Do not treat undiagnosed pigment with cryotherapy, IPL or laser.

pearls.t: Solar lentigines are a UV dosimeter — use the visit for skin-cancer education.
Hand spots are a classic patient question; same rules as the face.

Flat brown marks that become raised and warty are usually [seborrhoeic keratoses](condition:seborrhoeic-keratosis); a lentigo that darkens or spreads unevenly on the face may be [lentigo maligna](condition:melanoma).
